name: Zeta 2.1 (Zed edit prediction)
purpose: Zed Industries states: a code edit-prediction (next-edit suggestion) model; given code context, edit history and an editable region around the cursor it predicts the rewritten content of that region.

lineage.how_derived: fine-tune (model version 0323-multi-region-filtered-r3) with numbered multi-region markers

license.name: Apache-2.0 (card)
license.notes: Card says "License: Apache-2.0"; the repository has no LICENSE file (checked 2026-11-19). The base model Seed-Coder-8B-Base license was not read.

architecture.why_this_design: The card states no architecture reasons; it documents the prompt format (suffix-prefix-middle FIM tokens plus edit history and editable-region markers) the model was trained on.

engine_support.notes: Llama architecture; GGUFs exist (mradermacher, bartowski for zeta-2).

strengths: Purpose-built for next-edit prediction with Zed's prompt format
small enough (5 GB at Q4_K_M) to share a 16 GB GPU with a coder
weaknesses: No benchmark numbers on the card
prompt format is tied to Zed's editor protocol
soft.maturity: Zed Industries: zeta (2025-01), zeta-2, zeta-2.1; 2k downloads for 2.1, 517k for the first zeta.

tona_fit.reason: Right purpose for autocomplete next to the coder and Apache by card, but no quality numbers and an editor-specific prompt protocol; sweep-next-edit-1.5b is 3x smaller. Revisit with an autocomplete test plan (research/52).
blockers: Tona has no dense Llama module for 8B autocomplete serving (engine support, not quality)

open_questions: Edit-prediction quality against Sweep Next-Edit 1.5B: no comparison found. Check: both on one next-edit test set.
Seed-Coder-8B-Base license. Check: its LICENSE file.
Per-language quality: no public per-language numbers found. Check: our own polyglot run per language.
